Akaun is bookkeeping software for small teams and freelancers. You install it on your own server, so your books stay with you. Each user signs in from a web browser. Akaun keeps one list of records. Each record tells where money came from and where it went. AI can read your receipts, bills and bank statements and prepare the records for you. Akaun also makes quotations and invoices, matches your accounts to bank statements, and gives standard reports. Many users can work in one book, and each user gets only the permissions that you give. This guide is for the people who keep the books. It is also for the person who installs Akaun and manages its users and settings. Read Getting started first. Then read How Akaun works before you record a lot of data. Use the other sections when you need them. The Glossary gives the meaning of each term.

Getting started: install Akaun, sign in and prepare your book. How Akaun works: the ideas behind records, accounts, contacts and balances. Everyday tasks: record expenses, income, transfers and payments. Auto Import: let AI read receipts, statements and spreadsheets. Quotations and invoices: prepare quotations and invoices for your customers. Contacts: keep a list of the people and businesses that you work with. Bank reconciliation: check each account against the statement from the bank. Dashboard and reports: see how the business is doing. Administration: manage users, permissions, settings and the safety of your data. Help: answers to common problems, and the meaning of each term.

Use this page to keep a safe copy of your book, to restore it, and to install a new version of Akaun. Make a backup on a regular schedule, and always before an upgrade. info Akaun has no backup, restore or reset button in the screens. The description of the Administrators group mentions backups and reset, but these functions do not exist at this time. You make a backup when you copy files on the server.

Akaun keeps all the data of your book in two places. Copy both of them together. The database is the file at DATABASE_PATH. The default is data/akaun.db in the folder of the code. Two more files can be next to it: akaun.db-wal and akaun.db-shm. The three files are one database. The storage folder is the folder at STORAGE_PATH. The default is data/storage. It holds the receipts, attachments, statements and the company logo. With Docker, both are in the data folder next to docker-compose.yml. Copy the full data folder. Also keep a copy of your settings file: docker-compose.yml for Docker, or .env for an installation from the source code. See Where your data is.

Stop Akaun before you copy the files. While Akaun runs, it can write to the database at any time. The newest changes are often only in the -wal file. A copy of akaun.db alone can lose these changes. A copy made during a write can also be damaged. If you cannot stop Akaun, copy the three database files together, at a time when nobody uses Akaun. A copy of a running database is not fully safe.

Go to the folder that contains docker-compose.yml. Stop Akaun: docker compose stop Copy the full data folder to a different disk or computer, for example: cp -a data /backup/akaun-2026-10-09 Start Akaun again: docker compose start

Stop the server. Use the service manager of your server, or press Ctrl+C in the terminal of bun server.js. Copy the database file to a different disk or computer. If akaun.db-wal and akaun.db-shm are next to the database file, copy them too. Copy the storage folder. From the folder of the code, start the server again with bun server.js.

documents.t: The backup has the database file and the storage folder. Keep each backup with its date in the name. Keep one or more backups on a different computer from the server. tip To test a backup, restore it on a different computer and open Akaun there. A backup that you did not test can be incomplete.

caution A restore replaces all the data of the book with the backup. The changes that users made after the backup are lost. Before you restore, copy the current data to a different folder. Stop Akaun. Move the current database files and the storage folder to a different folder. Copy the database file of the backup to the location of DATABASE_PATH. If the backup has -wal and -shm files, copy them too. Make sure that no -wal or -shm file from the current data stays next to the database. Copy the storage folder of the backup to the location of STORAGE_PATH. Start Akaun. Sign in and do the ledger integrity check. See Check the book. The book shows the data at the time of the backup. With Docker, Akaun makes the user PUID the owner of the data folder each time it starts. Restore a backup only into the version of Akaun that made it, or a newer version. An older version cannot always read a database that a newer version changed.
caution Make a backup before each upgrade. A new version can change the database, and you cannot undo this change from inside Akaun. Keep the backup until you check the book with the new version.
Make a backup. See Make a backup. Go to the folder that contains docker-compose.yml. Get the new version: docker compose pull Start the new version: docker compose up -d

Make a backup. See Make a backup. Make sure that the server is stopped. In the folder of the code, get the new code: git pull Install the packages: bun install Build the application: bun run build Start the server: bun server.js

documents.t: A new version updates the database by itself when it starts for the first time. You do not type a command. Usually Akaun changes the database in place and keeps no copy. This is why your own backup is necessary. A book from an older version, from before the standard chart of accounts, needs a larger conversion. Akaun does this conversion on a copy of the database first: If all the checks pass, Akaun puts the converted copy in place. It moves the previous files into a new folder next to the database. The name of the folder is pre-chart- with the date and time, for example data/pre-chart-2026-10-09T08-15-30.123Z. The folder holds akaun.db, and akaun.db-wal and akaun.db-shm if they existed. If a check fails, Akaun does not start. The server shows This installation's books could not be converted, so the server has not started. Your database has not been changed. and the reason. Akaun does not use the pre-chart- folder again. After you check the book, you can move the folder to your backup storage. If the book is very old, Akaun does not start. The server tells you which version to install first. Install that version, start it one time, and then install the new version. Akaun does not change your database in this case.

documents.t: Do this check after each upgrade and after each restore. info You need the View permission on Reports to see the Books tab. A superuser can see it. In the sidebar, click Settings. Click the Books tab. Under Ledger integrity check, click Check now. If the tab shows Migration results, read each part of it. Open the Reports screen and compare the main figures with the figures before the upgrade. If all records balance, Akaun shows All good. Every record balances, and so does everything added up together. See Settings reference. Migration results can say that a copy of your data is in data/backups. This is not correct. The copy is in the pre-chart- folder next to the database. If a figure is wrong, do these steps: Stop Akaun. Restore the backup that you made before the upgrade. Install the previous version again. Report the problem. See Troubleshooting.

A backup copy holds all your financial data and the API keys of your AI providers. Keep it in a safe place. Akaun does not make backups on a schedule. Use the tools of your server, for example a cron job, to stop Akaun, copy the files and start Akaun again.

Akaun can give read-only data to an AI assistant that supports MCP (Model Context Protocol). Then you can ask the assistant questions about your books, for example "What did we spend on shipping in September?". The assistant reads the data. It cannot change the data.

The assistant can read these items. It reads only the areas where the user has the View permission. What the assistant can read Permission that the user needs The list of records, with filters for dates, kinds, accounts, categories, contacts, text, amounts, paid and cleared View on Records One record, with its lines. It can also read the settlements and the stored text of the documents. View on Records The statement of one account View on Records The outstanding amounts: what customers owe you, and what you owe View on Records The list of accounts, with their balances View on Accounts The list of contacts View on Contacts The balance of one contact View on Contacts and Records A report: Profit & Loss, Balance Sheet, Cash Flow Statement or Partners' Equity View on Reports The list of files on Auto Import, and the items of one file View on Auto Import Akaun also gives the assistant guidance for record descriptions. The assistant can use it to suggest better descriptions. You make each change by hand in Akaun. The assistant cannot add, change or delete anything. It cannot upload files, confirm imports, match bank lines or record payments. caution The assistant sends the data that it reads to the AI service of the assistant. This can include amounts, contact names, descriptions and the text of your receipts and bills. Connect an assistant only if you agree that this service can read this data. Give the assistant only the permissions that it needs.

With the sign-in (OAuth), the assistant opens Akaun in a browser. You sign in and choose what the assistant can read. Use this way when the assistant supports it. The administrator must enable it first. With an API token, you put an API token in the settings of the assistant. Use this way when the assistant cannot use the sign-in. In both ways, the server address is the address of Akaun with /mcp at the end, for example https://books.example.com/mcp.

For the sign-in way, the administrator must change two settings on the server: Set ORIGIN to the public HTTPS address of Akaun, for example https://books.example.com. Add the setting OAUTH_ENABLED=true. Start Akaun again. See Install Akaun. ORIGIN must start with https://. Only a localhost or 127.0.0.1 address can use http://. Do not put a path after the address. If the address is not correct, Akaun does not start, and the server log tells why. An assistant that runs in the cloud must reach your server from the internet. If you use a reverse proxy, it must send the paths /mcp, /oauth/ and /.well-known/ to Akaun. The API token way needs no change on the server.

caution The app sends its own name. Akaun does not check it. Connect only from an assistant that you started yourself. If you did not start the connection, click Cancel. In the assistant, add a new MCP server. The name of this function is different in each assistant, for example "connector" or "integration". Type the server address, for example https://books.example.com/mcp. Choose OAuth as the type of authentication. If Akaun asks you to sign in, sign in. On the Connect page, read the app name and the Client ID. Clear each permission that you do not want to give. Click Allow selected access. The assistant can now read your data. The app shows on your profile, on the Connected apps tab. The page shows each permission that the app asks for, from this list: Read records, statements and outstanding amounts Read accounts and balances Read contacts Read financial reports Read import jobs and extracted documents Akaun selects each permission that you have. If you do not have a permission, the page shows Your account does not have this permission. and you cannot select it. If you clear all the permissions, Akaun shows Select at least one available permission. Click Cancel to refuse the connection. A connection stays valid for 30 days or less. Then connect the assistant again.

caution An API token can do more than read. Through the API of Akaun, a program with the token can do all the actions that the user can do, also changes and deletes. Do not use the token of a superuser. Make a separate user that can only view. As a superuser, make a group that has only View on the areas that the assistant needs. See Make a group. Add a user for the assistant, in this group only. See Add a user. Issue an API token for this user. See Issue an API token for a user. In the assistant, add a new MCP server of the type "Streamable HTTP". Type the server address, for example https://books.example.com/mcp. Add the header Authorization with the value Bearer and the token, for example Bearer akn_1234…. The assistant can now read the data that the user can view.

If you connected with the sign-in, open your profile, click Connected apps, and click Revoke access for the app. See Your profile. If you connected with an API token, revoke the token. See Replace or remove a token. The assistant stops immediately. A new password also disconnects all the apps of the user that connected with the sign-in. Sign out does not disconnect them.

Akaun checks the permissions of the user on each request. If you remove a permission from the group, the assistant loses that data on its next request. With the sign-in, a superuser is also limited to the permissions that the superuser selected. The assistant reads the data at the time of its question. It does not get live updates. A list gives 50 rows at a time by default, and 200 rows at the most. A statement gives 500 lines or fewer. For a long period, ask about a shorter period. Use HTTPS for a connection over the internet. An API token sent over plain HTTP is not safe.
A permission lets a user do one action in one area of Akaun. Read this page before you make a group or give a user extra permissions. To change the permissions, see Users and groups.

View: open the screen of the area and see its items. Without View, the screen does not open, and its item does not show in the sidebar. Add: make a new item. Change: change an item that exists. Delete: remove an item. A superuser has all the actions in all the areas. The permission grid does not apply to a superuser.

The permission grid in Users & Groups shows these areas. The table tells what each action lets a user do. "No effect" shows that Akaun does not use the action in that area.
